Order 
This criminal revision petition is filed against the conviction and sentence imposed on the revision petitioner as per the judgment dated 09.08.2012 in CC No.548/2008 by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Perinthalmanna and the judgment dated 03.06.2017 in Crl. Appeal No.242/2012 by the Additional Sessions Court-II, Manjeri.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Perinthalmanna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It was a prosecution initiated by the Sub- Inspector of Police, Melattur, alleging offences punishable under Sections 420, 463, 465 & 468 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The prosecution case in brief is as follows: on 11.6.2005 at 09:00 am, accused Nos.1 and 2 in the charge sheet came to the house of the de facto complainant in Kizhattur Amsom Mulliamkurussi desom.
The accused No.1 made the defacto complainant believe that he had arranged a visa for going abroad.
By dishonestly representing to the defacto complainant that he is in need of money for the purpose of a visa, accused No.1 borrowed Rs.40,000/- from the defacto complainant.

At that time, accused 2025:KER:73752 CRL.REV.PET NO.716 OF 2023 No.1 had executed and issued a cheque bearing No.219361 to the defacto complainant, making him believe that it was a cheque drawn on his account and that there was sufficient amount in the account.

When the defacto complainant presented the cheque through South Malabar Gramin Bank, Kizhattur, it was returned V.M. Janardhanan vs State Of Kerala on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31948880/
2 dishonoured with a memo showing the reason 'there is a difference in the signature of the drawer'.

entities.text: V.M. Janardhanan vs State Of Kerala on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Later, the defacto complainant realised that both the accused, in furtherance of their common intention to cheat the defacto complainant, had issued a cheque drawn on the account maintained by accused No.2 by putting the signature of accused No.1.
Thereby, both the accused dishonestly induced the defacto complainant to advance an amount of Rs. 40,000/- to the accused.
Thus, the accused have committed forgery in respect of the cheque by signing the cheque of the second accused.
The accused has committed forgery for the purpose of cheating.
Thus, the accused herein is alleged to have committed the offences punishable under sections 420, 463, 465, 468 r/w 34 IPC along with accused No.2 in the charge sheet.

3. After going through the evidence and documents produced by the prosecution, the trial court found that, the accused is guilty under Sections 420, 463, 465 & 468 r/w Section 2025:KER:73752 CRL.REV.PET NO.716 OF 2023 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
The sentence was also imposed for the offences.
4. Aggrieved by the conviction and sentence, an appeal was filed before the Appellate Court.
The appeal was considered by the Additional Sessions Judge-II, Manjeri.
The appeal was dismissed by confirming the conviction and sentence.
Aggrieved by the same, this revision is filed.
5. When this revision came up for consideration, the counsel for the petitioner submitted that the dispute between the petitioner and the victims in this case is already settled.
An affidavit is filed by the defacto complainant and one of the victims, as evident by Annexures-A1 and A2.
This Court directed the Public Prosecutor to get a statement of the victims through the Investigating Officer.
Today, the Public Prosecutor submitted that the statement is recorded and the victims have no grievance against the petitioner.
If that is the case, I think the continuation of the conviction and sentence is not necessary.
This Court can exercise inherent jurisdiction and set aside the conviction and sentence.

Therefore, this criminal revision petition is allowed in the following manner:
2025:KER:73752 CRL.REV.PET NO.716 OF 2023 1.

The conviction and sentence imposed on the revision petitioner as per the judgment dated 09.08.2012 in CC No.548/2008 by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Perinthalmanna and the judgment dated 03.06.2017 in Crl.
Appeal No.242/2012 by the Additional Sessions Court-II, Manjeri, are set aside, and the revision petitioner is acquitted.
